youtube.title: Romans washed their clothes in pee. The emperor taxed it 🤢 #shorts
youtube.caption:
Ancient Romans really did clean their clothes with pee. 🤢 And the emperor found a way to tax it.

Would you wear the pee toga for clean clothes? Yes or no 👇

Parody · fictional chat. Based on history: Roman fullers (laundry workers) used stale urine, rich in ammonia, to clean and whiten wool. They collected it from pots left on street corners, and Emperor Vespasian put a tax on urine collected from public latrines. When his son complained, Vespasian held up a coin: "pecunia non olet" — money doesn't smell.
